claims.evidence: Let p≥1 zombies guarantee capture in t rounds. If a vertex v were initially farther than t from every zombie, the survivor could start at v and remain stationary; unit-speed zombies could not reach v by round t. Hence the radius-t balls around the initial zombie positions cover all n^k vertices. Each L1 ball lies in an L∞ cube of at most (2t+1)^k vertices, so n^k≤p(2t+1)^k. With x=p+t, p≤x and, since p≥1 and t≥0, 2t+1≤3x. Therefore n^k≤3^k x^(k+1), giving x≥3^(-k/(k+1))n^(k/(k+1)). This applies to every admissible p and therefore to the throttling minimum. The argument is valid for every fixed k≥1, including t=0.
claims.search_method: Independent covering-necessity proof, followed by exact-integer testing of the finite algebraic implication over 1,853,871 parameter instances.

claims.claim: Mesh capture lemma: for each r≥1 there are constants M_r,A_r such that, on every r-dimensional Cartesian grid with coordinate meshes containing both endpoints and having gaps at most d, placing M_r zombies at every mesh intersection guarantees capture in at most A_r d rounds.
claims.evidence: The induction is sound with M_1=A_1=1, M_r=2rM_(r-1), and A_r=(r+1)(A_(r-1)+1). In dimension one, the two mesh zombies bracketing an unoccupied survivor remain barriers and move inward every zombie turn, so capture occurs within the interval length, at most d. For the induction step put R=A_(r-1)d. On either side in coordinate i, if the boundary is at distance below R it is an eligible mesh hyperplane; otherwise the gap bound supplies a mesh hyperplane at distance in [R,R+d). Each of the 2r labeled hyperplanes receives M_(r-1) zombies at each projected mesh point. The factor 2r supplies disjoint teams even at intersections. Applying the lower-dimensional strategy to the survivor's projection is legitimate: every projected zombie move decreases the full L1 distance by one. By round R each team supplies a zombie matching every survivor coordinate except i. A nonboundary plane initially at distance at least R cannot be passed before this; in the tight distance-R case, entry on the R-th survivor move either lands on the already aligned zombie or projection capture has already produced the guard. Boundaries cannot be passed. Once established, an i-guard repairs the sole projected mismatch if the survivor just moved in another coordinate; otherwise it advances in coordinate i. Each prescribed move is shortest-path legal, and the guard is aligned before every subsequent survivor turn, so crossing it causes capture. After all guards are aligned, let W be the sum of the r lower-to-upper guard separations. Guard motion during setup cannot increase these separations, and initially W<2r(R+d). A survivor move in coordinate j makes precisely the two j-guards advance inward while all other guards repair coordinate j, decreasing W by two; a stationary move decreases it still faster. Thus capture takes at most r(R+d)=r(A_(r-1)+1)d additional rounds. Including setup and one alignment round gives R+1+r(A_(r-1)+1)d≤A_rd because the difference is d−1≥0. Singleton-grid degeneracies are captured immediately.
claims.witness: Constructive constants M_1=A_1=1, M_r=2rM_(r-1), A_r=(r+1)(A_(r-1)+1), together with the 2r projected-hyperplane teams and maintained lower/upper guards.
claims.search_method: Reconstructed the induction from scratch and audited team allocation, projection legality, boundary and exact-R crossing cases, acquisition timing, guard sidedness, and the potential decrease. Supplemented this proof with exact exhaustive checks of 32 path lengths, 139,560 mesh-selection cases, and 64,584 guard transitions.

claims.claim: Consequently, for every fixed k≥3, th_z((P_n)^{□k})=Θ_k(n^{k/(k+1)})=Θ_k(|G|^{1/(k+1)}); in particular the k=3 endpoint is complete.
claims.evidence: Use in every coordinate the endpoint-containing mesh formed by multiples of d plus n−1. It has gaps at most d and at most n/d+2 points, so Claim 1 gives p≤M_k(n/d+2)^k and capture time at most A_kd. For d=ceil(n^(k/(k+1))), d≥n^(k/(k+1)), so n/d≤n^(1/(k+1)); also d≤n^(k/(k+1))+1≤2n^(k/(k+1)). Consequently both p and the capture time are O_k(n^(k/(k+1))). For sufficiently large n this placement uses at most n^k zombies; the finitely many remaining n are handled by occupying every vertex and do not affect the asymptotic bound. Combining this upper bound with Claim 0 gives Θ_k(n^(k/(k+1))). Since |G|=n^k, this equals Θ_k(|G|^(1/(k+1))). Exact recurrence evaluation gives M_3=24 and A_3=28, so the claimed explicit k=3 strategy and the requested first endpoint follow.
claims.witness: For k=3, take d=ceil(n^(3/4)); the construction uses at most 24(n/d+2)^3 zombies and captures within 28d rounds. The same recurrence supplies fixed constants for every fixed k≥3.
claims.search_method: Checked the mesh cardinality and asymptotic optimization symbolically, verified the p≤|G| issue for asymptotic use, and ran exact-integer recurrence and ceiling-power checks for 480 finite (n,k) cases.

Because |G|=n^k, the exponent is exactly the requested one, and k=3 is explicitly included with concrete constants. Thus the entire target is resolved at the requested matching asymptotic strength.
